finding.claim: The admin check on the ban route is bypassed. require_admin aborts with 403, but the bare except Exception at admin.py:18 swallows the abort, logs it, and proceeds to do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20.
finding.source: admin.py:14-15 POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban; uid taken from the URL path and not validated. Caller identity comes from g.user, which the repo does not set.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (currently a stub at admin.py:31-32)

trace.note: For a non-admin, abort(403) raises an HTTPException, which subclasses Exception
bare except Exception catches the HTTPException (and an AttributeError if g.user is missing)
only a log.warning is emitted; no re-raise or return
do_ban(uid) runs for the non-admin caller

finding.guards_checked: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) is enforced but its exception is discarded. No route decorator or before_request guard in the repo. The sibling unban route (admin.py:24-28) calls require_admin outside any try block, so its 403 propagates and it is SAFE. Whether g.user is populated for unauthenticated callers is UNCERTAIN because the auth middleware is not in this repo.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) is the only check, and it aborts with 403, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception at admin.py:16-19. The except block only logs and does not re-raise or return, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 still runs. No route decorator or before_request guard exists in this repo. The unban route (admin.py:26) calls require_admin outside any try, so it is not affected.
verdict.reason: For a caller whose g.user is a dict without is_admin, require_admin at admin.py:11 raises HTTPException (a subclass of Exception), the except at admin.py:18 swallows it, and do_ban(uid) runs at admin.py:20, so the ban route's authorization is bypassed. The trace is wrong in one sub-claim: at admin.py:17-19, if g.user is missing entirely, the AttributeError is caught at line 18 but line 19 evaluates g.user.get again, which raises an uncaught AttributeError, so do_ban is not reached in that case. The core non-admin bypass is accurate, and the attacker needs only an authenticated low-privilege session (or any caller whose g.user lacks is_admin), so the finding holds, though the trace's AttributeError note should be corrected. Minor wording: the handler is `except Exception`, not a bare except.
